goal: Give contract validation and the automated driver ONE canonical verification-command grammar, owned by the canonical contract module, so a contract whose sealed verification plan the driver cannot execute is refused at seal/validation time instead of sealing cleanly and failing closed later during review.
non_goals: Widening the executable grammar to new forms — no `node <script>`, no multi-path `npx <bin> run <a> <b>`, no shell, no chaining. This task makes validation agree with the driver; it does not give the driver more reach
Changing what the driver EXECUTES: the spawn path, `shell: false`, the node_modules copy, the environment allowlist and the tracked-at-head path checks in tools/review-task.mjs are untouched
Changing the refusal semantics at execution time — an unsupported command must still be refused by the executor, because a contract sealed before this change can still contain one
Re-sealing, migrating or editing any existing contract in .agent/tasks/**
Changing the contract schema: no new field, no removed field, no change to BINDING_FIELDS or the digest computation
Changing tier definitions, ALWAYS_FORBIDDEN, PROTECTED_CONTROL_PLANE, CONTROL_PLANE_GRANTS, covers() or the path grammar
Touching .claude/hooks/**, .claude/settings.json or runtime-scope.test.mjs — the runtime policy is a separate authority boundary and is under active change on another branch
Touching docs/AUTOMATION-AUTHORITY.md — it is being edited by the FAB-58 branch and must not be edited concurrently
Closing the bare-subtree-root gap in covers() (FAB-60) or any other opportunistic validator fix
Any product, database, Supabase, src/ or workflow change
acceptance_criteria: The verification grammar is defined in exactly one place. tools/review-protocol.mjs no longer defines it and instead re-exports it, so tools/review-task.mjs and review-protocol.test.mjs keep working through their existing import paths with no change to those import sites

The definition lives in tools/verify-task-contracts.mjs, which review-protocol.mjs already imports from, so no import cycle is created — verified by a spec that the dependency runs in one direction only

findContractViolations refuses any verification entry that parseVerificationCommand cannot turn into an execution plan, and the violation message carries the parser's own refusal reason rather than a restatement of it

The npm-script-existence check derives the script name from the parsed plan rather than from a second regex, so the two cannot drift. A spec pins the specific drift that exists today: a script name the old validator regex accepted but the driver grammar refuses
Every contract currently sealed in .agent/tasks/** still validates — asserted by a spec that parses each one's verification entries, not by running the CLI once by hand
Agreement is proven in BOTH directions by specs: every command the validator accepts yields a non-null driver plan, and every command the driver refuses produces a validator violation
The refusal is enforced at seal time too: sealing a contract carrying an unsupported verification command fails rather than writing a digest over it
docs/REVIEWER-PROTOCOL.md no longer states that the contract validator does not constrain verification commands, and says where the single grammar now lives and what still happens at execution time
npm run verify:tasks reports every contract valid
stop_conditions: Moving the grammar turns out to require changing tools/review-task.mjs or any import site outside allowed_paths — report rather than widening

An existing sealed contract in .agent/tasks/** turns out to carry a verification command the driver cannot execute, so tightening the validator would invalidate it — STOP and report, because re-sealing an existing contract is a non-goal and the migration is a root-governance decision
Removing the definition from tools/review-protocol.mjs breaks a consumer that a re-export cannot satisfy — report before changing that consumer
The work turns out to need a control_plane grant — report; tools/** is Tier 2 and this contract declares none
The work turns out not to fit workflow-authority / r3 / none — report before implementing
notes: FAB-57, filed from the fresh review of PR #234 (FAB-56). FAB-56 sealed a contract containing `npx vitest run task-contract.test.mjs review-protocol.test.mjs` and `node tools/verify-task-contracts.mjs`; the validator accepted both, while the driver's VERIFICATION_FORMS grammar refuses both — the two-path npx form and the `node <script>` form are outside it. The contract sealed cleanly and would have failed closed at review time instead. Reconnaissance for this contract: all 8 currently sealed contracts were run through parseVerificationCommand and every command parses, so tightening the validator invalidates nothing and no migration is needed. A second, narrower instance of the same drift was found while reading: the validator's own npm-script-existence check uses /^npm run ([\w:-]+)$/ while the driver uses /^npm run ([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9:_-]*)$/, so a script named `_internal` satisfies the validator's check and is refused by the driver — the same class of mismatch one level down, which is why the fix derives the name from the parsed plan instead of matching twice. Direction of the move matters: review-protocol.mjs already imports from verify-task-contracts.mjs, so importing the grammar the other way would create a cycle; the grammar moves down into the canonical contract module and is re-exported upward. Classification: workflow-authority because this is harness/control-plane machinery; r3 by the convention every other tools/ harness contract in this repository uses; production_effect none because nothing here is bundled, shipped or run against production — verify-task-contracts.mjs and review-protocol.mjs are developer/CI tooling.
